newsitem.title: USA: Nash Finch Q1 hurt by Midwest flood.
newsitem.headline: Nash Finch Q1 hurt by Midwest flood.

text.p: Nash Finch Co said Monday that several factors hurt its first quarter results, including flooding in the Midwest.

"Overall, the results for the first quarter were good, especially when one considers that our operations in the Midwest were adversely affected by the severe winter weather conditions experienced in the Upper Midwest, followed by record flooding -- not only in the Red River Valley area of Minnesota and North Dakota where the impact is still being felt, but also in southwestern Minnesota, Ohio and Kentucky," Al Flaten, president of the food wholesaler said.

Higher debt as a result of acquisition financing, expenses related to the continuing design and development of the company's new information system, and amortization expense due to goodwill associated with 1996 acquisitions, also hurt net income in the quarter, the company said.
Nash finch earlier Monday reported net income of $3.1 million, or $0.27 a share, compared to $2.8 million, or $0.26 a share, a year ago.
